title: Afar Hilib Ari (Spiced Camel Meat)
community: Afar people — nomadic pastoralists of the northeastern desert
author: Chef Haile

heritage.origin: Afar people — the Afar Triangle, one of the world's most extreme environments
heritage.history: The Afar are a nomadic pastoralist people living in one of the world's most extreme environments — the Afar Triangle, which includes the Danakil Depression (the hottest place on earth). Their cuisine is entirely adapted to nomadic life: camel and goat meat, camel milk, dates, and dried foods that can be transported. Hilib Ari (camel meat stew) is the most prestigious Afar dish — camel meat is expensive and valued, prepared for weddings, religious celebrations, and important guests. The Afar use a spice mixture called berbere that differs significantly from Amhara berbere, featuring more cumin and coriander.

desc: Afar Hilib Ari — camel (or beef) slow-cooked for 3 hours with Afar spices: cumin, coriander, turmeric, and ginger. The nomadic desert feast — camel meat requires long cooking and rewards with extraordinary depth. Made for weddings and significant celebrations.
longDesc: Hilib Ari is the Afar prestige dish — camel meat, slow-cooked until tender with the Afar spice tradition that emphasises cumin and coriander over berbere. The harsh desert environment has produced a cuisine of remarkable efficiency.
ingredients: 1.2kg camel meat (or beef as substitute) — cut into large chunks
steps: Brown onions in oil until very golden.
Add garlic, ginger, cumin, coriander, turmeric, and pepper.
Add camel meat (or beef). Brown 5 minutes.
Add water. Simmer covered 2.5—3 hours (camel) or 90 minutes (beef).
Meat should be very tender. Season.
chefTips: Camel meat requires much longer cooking than beef.
commonMistakes: Under-cooking camel — very tough if not fully cooked.
cookingScience: Camel meat has a higher collagen content in its connective tissue than beef — requiring longer braising to convert collagen to gelatine. The resulting sauce is extraordinarily rich when properly cooked.
sustainabilityTips: Camel is the most sustainable large animal for desert environments — requiring far less water than cattle.
servedWith: Rice (Afar prefer rice with this dish)
healthBenefits: Camel meat is lower in fat than beef.
culturalNote: Afar Hilib Ari is the wedding feast of the desert — prepared when a family wants to honour guests with the most precious protein available in the Afar Triangle. The camel that is slaughtered for a wedding feast represents a significant sacrifice.
